title: Oncall diary: thermal spikes, driver rollbacks, and interconnect flutters
summary: First-person on-call log capturing an 36-hour instability window where small ECC bursts and thermal excursions preceded NVLink renegotiation and driver OOPS. Includes ad-hoc mitigations, quick experiments (driver rollbacks, perf limits), and a draft runbook checklist for quarantine and repro steps.
body:
Purpose and context:
This is a working on-call diary and runbook sketch capturing the sequence, ad-hoc mitigations, and next-step experiments from the 2026-10-11 through 2026-10-13 instability window affecting a subset of our GPU nodes in cluster-gamma. The goal is to preserve the chronology, commands, heuristics we tried, and a compact runbook for the nightshift team to iterate on.

High level summary of incident window:
- Symptoms: intermittent kernel panics in compute pods (oom-like backtraces), driver OOPS logs on host, and NVLink link renegotiation events. Observed short-lived increases in correctable ECC counts on affected DIMMs prior to link flaps.
- Impact: several model Serving jobs were evicted or failed with degraded tail latency. Two nodes quarantined for manual investigation.
- Hypothesis (working): thermal boundary crossing + a driver scheduling race triggers transient MMU/KVM faults that show as kernel panic/OOPS; ECC bursts are correlated but may be symptomatic of bus noise or voltage/temperature transitions rather than primary memory degradation. NVLink renegotiation appears as the outward failure mode as the system tries to recover.

Chronological on-call log (local timestamps UTC):
2026-10-11 21:45 - Pager fires (INC-GPU-3942): multiple pods on node gamma-13 restarting.
- Slack snippet: "gamma-13 tail by logs shows: nvidia: GPU HANG, GPU reset required, kernel panic trace with GPU-linked stack"
- Quick checks: ssh into gamma-13, dmesg shows repeated: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus" and NVLink: "link status change - negotiation failed".
- Commands run:
  - sudo dmesg | tail -n 120 -> grabbed kernel OOPS fragments.
  - nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,temperature.gpu,driver_version,pstate --format=csv
  - nvidia-smi --query-gpu=ecc.errors.corrected.volatile.memory --format=csv
  - journalctl -k --since "30 minutes ago" | grep -i nvlink
- Observations: GPU temp 83 C on gpu0, driver v543.12, ECC corrected counters show tiny bursts: 3->12 correctables in last 10 minutes (per-sample).

2026-10-11 22:10 - Node quarantined and workload drained
- Action: cordon gamma-13, drain pods to gamma-21 and gamma-37 using kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data.
- Rationale: preserve node for postmortem; minimize user impact.

2026-10-12 00:05 - Similar symptoms observed on gamma-21 but less severe
- gamma-21 showed NVLink negotiation warnings in dmesg and a single driver OOPS then recovered. No full kernel panic.
- Compared ECC counters between gamma-13 (quarantined, persisted logs) and gamma-21 (live): gamma-13 had higher transient spikes.

2026-10-12 01:30 - Ad-hoc mitigation: throttled power and reduced fan curves via BMC for one node
- Why: quick attempt to see if reducing thermal swing influences recurrence.
- Commands and notes: we used IPMI/BMC API to raise fan profile and lower power-limit for affected GPU via nvidia-smi -pl 250 (from 300). Observed downstream drop in temp to ~74 C within 6 minutes.
- Result: thermal mitigation temporarily suppressed repeat failure for ~2 hours on gamma-21.

2026-10-12 04:10 - Driver rollback test planned
- Rationale: kernel OOPS stack traces reference driver regions changed between 530.x and 543.x. We planned a controlled rollback to 530.41 on a single spare node (gamma-spare-05) and synthetic workload to stress NVLink.
- Steps executed:
  - Installed driver 530.41 via package and dkms rebuild, rebooted host.
  - Launched intra-node nvlink stress harness (simple memory-write/read patterns + inter-GPU memcpy with pinned CPU threads).
- Result: no NVLink renegotiation for 24 hours under same synthetic load; ECC counters remained low. This is a useful signal but inconclusive.

Observed artifacts and logs of interest (copied excerpts):
- Kernel OOPS snippet: "[   12.345678] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
  [   12.345680] kernel: RIP: 0010:0x... <nvidia_uvm_query_mmap>+0x...
  [   12.345685] ---[ end trace ... ]---
  [   12.345687] nvlink: negotiation timeout on link 1
"
- ECC counter delta samples (minute resolution): gamma-13 gpu0: 0 -> 4 -> 9 -> 28 -> 30 in 9 minutes before panic.
- NVLink event frequency correlated to temp crossing 80C in 7/8 samples.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Thermal cycling crosses a retimer/PHY threshold causing transient link errors; driver/firmware paths then hit an unhandled state that results in a kernel OOPS.
2) Driver regression in v54x series exposes a race when NVLink renegotiation occurs during active DMA, leading to MMU map invalid access (observed in trace).
3) Underlying memory DIMM is marginal, producing bursts of correctable ECC that cascade into GPU fault (less likely given ECC counters return to baseline on other nodes under identical workload).

Quick experiments and results (for reproducibility):
- Driver rollback to 530.41 on spare node with synthetic stress: stable for 24h.
- Thermal throttling (lower PL and higher fans): reduced incident frequency in two tested nodes.
- Isolated NVLink: disabled NVLink between two GPUs (bios/slot configuration) and ran same workload; no kernel OOPS observed in short run (6 hours).

Ad-hoc mitigations used during the window (operational playbook candidate):
- Immediate: cordon and drain node, increase fan profile, reduce GPU power-limit, move critical workloads off potentially affected nodes.
- Short-term: scale up capacity on healthy nodes, enable forced driver rollback on quarantine nodes for extended soak testing.
- Medium-term: schedule firmware (retimer/BIOS) and driver downgrade test matrix across subset of fleet during low usage window.

Draft runbook checklist (to iterate into formal playbook):
1) Triage initial alert: collect dmesg, nvidia-smi snapshot, ECC counters, ipmitool sensor list, pci-e topology (lspci -vv).
2) If kernel panic observed: cordon node, collect crashdump and preserve host.
3) If NVLink/negotiation warnings present but no panic: temporarily migrate critical pods and raise fan profile and lower power-limit by 10-20%.
4) If ECC corrected spikes present (>10 correctables/min on sustained sample): schedule immediate diagnostic memory scrub and mark node for deeper hardware validation.
5) For nodes with recurring NVLink flaps: run driver rollback to 530.41 in a control node and run the nvlink stress harness for 24h.
6) If driver rollback reduces incidents, plan fleet-level staged rollback or coordinate with driver vendor for a fix.
7) Document and tag relevant logs in JIRA and Confluence; attach kernel traces and nvlink logs.

Open action items and experiments (ownership suggestions):
- Run retimer firmware audit across fleet (owner: Marcus Liu).
- Build automated ECC burst detector that triggers early migration at lower thresholds (owner: Samir Rao).
- Run controlled driver-version canary rollout: 530.41 -> compare with current GA weekly; record mux of kernel OOPS presence (owner: Riley Chen).
- Engage HW vendor about NVLink negotiation corner cases at elevated temps and provide sample kernel traces (owner: Aisha Patel).

Notes, questions and things to watch for:
- Are ECC bursts a leading indicator (e.g., bus noise) vs trailing symptom? We need dense telemetry (1s resolution) at time of events to know.
- Confirm whether node thermal sensors (board-level) differ from GPU-reported temperature; we've seen a 5-7C delta in some racks.
- Consider enabling periodic ECC scrubbing if hardware supports it and we can tolerate overhead.

Appendix: useful commands and artifacts to collect (copy/paste friendly)
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,temperature.gpu,driver_version,pstate,utilization.gpu --format=csv -l 1
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=ecc.errors.corrected.volatile.memory,ecc.errors.uncorrected.volatile.memory --format=csv -l 1
- sudo dmesg --ctime --level=err,alert,crit | tail -n 200
- journalctl -k --since "1 hour ago" | egrep -i "nvrm|nvlink|gpu hang|Xid|NVRM"
- ipmitool sensor list | egrep -i "temp|fan|power|voltage"
- lspci -vvv | grep -A5 -i "NVIDIA"

Closing notes:
This diary is intentionally informal and contains raw hypotheses and commands we ran during the incident. The driver-rollback signal and thermal correlation are the strongest immediate leads. Next step is to formalize the runbook checklist above, run the firmware audit, and coordinate a measured canary of driver 530.41 across a small subset of GPU nodes during a controlled window.

If you update this doc, please append an edit header with your name and UTC timestamp and move resolved action items into the JIRA ticket JIRA-GPU-3942 for tracking.

-- Riley (oncall) 2026-10-14 09:12 UTC
